about: How AME writes a system's scope, as data: for the AI when it writes a system the Master Template has no entry for, or adds a line beyond the template's options, and for checking what it writes. Taken from the Master Template's 'Scope of Work Format' and 'How to use this template' sections and from system_templates.json. Edit here, never in code.

no_verb_starts.about: Line openings the Master Template itself writes without a verb (its no_verb lines and the front end's heading). 'starts' is what the AI is told (an interlock, a tie-in, low-voltage wiring); 'also_accepted' passes the check too (mapping points, monitoring, the integration rep line, relocation work). Any line the Master Template writes word for word also passes, whatever its opening.

lines: Furnish BMS Communication Wiring to {what} Factory Controls
Map Available Points Via Mfr. Provided BMS Interface
AME requires mfr. Rep to assist in integration, cost to be incurred by mech contractor
applies_when: the unit comes with the manufacturer's own (factory) controls
the manufacturer provides a gateway or BMS interface (BACnet, Modbus, LonWorks)
the evidence says to map the unit's points through the manufacturer's interface
integration_trio.rule: The three lines go together, in this order; {what} names the equipment (Chiller, Pump VFD, …) or is left out for plain factory controls. They replace the lines that name a DDC controller.

notes.rule: A note starting with "**" is only for a clarification to the client that the evidence supports, such as "**Start/Stop via Fire Alarm System" or "**Refrigeration Leak Detection system is coming with the unit per equipment schedule". Never an estimating hint (where to look, how to decide), tech hours or prices.
examples: **Refrigeration Leak Detection system is coming with the unit per equipment schedule
notes.by_unit_mfr_about: A note longer than 'long' characters saying a device comes with the unit, or is furnished by the unit's manufacturer, is shortened to this house form (the item in capitals) rather than dropped.

forbidden.about: Never in a line, a header or a note: the client sees these. Words are matched ignoring case; category words as whole words in capitals; patterns ignoring case.

guide: Each system is a block: a header "Qty (#) System Header" (the count, the kind of equipment, then the tags), then its scope lines.

Each scope line starts with a verb: Furnish and Install ABC; Furnish ABC; Furnish and Wire ABC; Install and Wire ABC (Furnished by Unit Mfr.); Install ABC (Furnished by Unit Mfr.); Wire ABC (Furnished by Unit Mfr.).
Details go after the device in brackets: (Qty. ## Total), (as per sequence), (Location: 3rd Floor), (Furnished by Unit Mfr.).
A clarification for the client is a note starting with "**", such as "**Start/Stop via Fire Alarm System".

When the unit comes with factory controls, the three integration lines go together: Furnish BMS Communication Wiring to Factory Controls; Map Available Points Via Mfr. Provided BMS Interface; and, one level in, AME requires mfr. Rep to assist in integration, cost to be incurred by mech contractor.
This is guidance, not a bible: it shows how a system is presented.
The points under a system are written from the control information the job gives. It is never a mandatory point list: in a real job the points follow that job's own control information.

line_order.about: How AME orders a system's lines: the controller first, then the sensors, then the points, then the valves and dampers, then the integration lines, then the notes. A line is put in the first group whose patterns it matches, in 'checked_in_this_order'; 'device' patterns look only at the device the line names (after the verb, before 'for', 'to', 'with', a bracket or a dash). A line no group matches stays next to the line above it. A sub-line moves with its parent. Patterns are regular expressions, ignoring case.

software_points.about: A 'Furnish …' line naming one of these is a software point, never a hardware point, for tech hours counted per hardware point.

sow_positions.about: The GEM's SOW ORDER — STANDARD TEMPLATE: the order of the categories of a block's lines, positions 1 to 20 (20, the miscellaneous responsibilities, are printed as '**' notes at the end of the block). A line takes the position of the first entry below it matches, in this order: 'verbs' are the openings it may start with (any when absent); it matches when one of the 'text' patterns is in the whole line or one of the 'device' patterns is in the device it names (after the verb, before a bracket or 'to'/'for'/'with'); an entry with neither matches on its verb alone. A line no entry matches (an interlock, a monitoring line) stays next to the line above it, never after the integration lines. Sub-lines move with their line. Regular expressions, ignoring case.

positions.name: Fire alarm and life safety wire lines
Furnish and wire: filter DP switches
Furnish and wire: valves and actuators
Hardwired furnish signals: fans and pumps
Miscellaneous responsibilities (printed as '**' notes at the end of the block)

panels.about: A system with no tags whose header or kind names a panel or a controller counts panels on its header (Qty (1), or the number of panels its quote states); the devices it counts go on the device line as (Qty. N Total). Patterns are regular expressions, ignoring case.

spec_openings.about: Specification wording at the start of a line ("ATC Contractor to provide …") is written in the house verb form; a line whose verb has no house form goes to the review list. 'patterns' find the opening; 'verbs' map the specification's verb to the house verb. Regular expressions, ignoring case.

internal.about: What the estimator's GEM writes for the estimator that the client must never see: its flag glyphs, the source ids of the job's documents, its word for the controls contractor ('CC', which the proposal writes 'AME'), its reasoning words and a label written twice. Checked on every header, line, note and exception the proposal prints. 'glyphs' and 'source_ids' are taken out; 'contractor' is replaced; a note naming one of 'words' or 'patterns' is never printed (it stays in the Evidence Package). Regular expressions, ignoring case, except 'contractor'.

clarifications.about: Which '*' and '**' notes the client sees. A '**' note prints only when it gives an item to the owner or to another party (another trade, the unit's manufacturer, others) or is one of the Master Template's own '**' clarifications; a '*' note only when it says who furnishes, installs or wires, or is an integral-thermostat or manufacturer-switch note. A note restating the controls contractor's software work ('**Program …', '**Set up …') never prints: it stays in the Evidence Package. 'parties' find another party ('ours' are the controls contractor's own names, which never count); 'unit_notes' find the integral-thermostat and manufacturer-switch notes; 'software_work' the openings of a note restating software work. Regular expressions, ignoring case.

unit_maker_devices.about: A device the unit's manufacturer furnishes, named in the GEM's exclusions for a system, prints in that block as '*<NAME> BY UNIT MFR.' (the estimator's form) instead of going to the review list. An exclusion counts when it names one of the devices and says the manufacturer or the unit furnishes it ('maker'); one saying the device comes with another unit ('with the rooftop units' in a VAV block) does not. Regular expressions, ignoring case.

misc_monitoring.about: The monitor-only systems (plumbing pumps, water heaters, water heat pumps, glycol, gas booster, heat tracing, a generator) are gathered as stacked headers under one block, as the Master Template's 'Misc Monitoring Systems' is written, when each has fewer than 'max_lines' + 1 lines and no controller of its own ('own_controller' in one of its lines). 'kinds' find such a system by its header or kind. Regular expressions, ignoring case.
misc_monitoring.devices_about: A planned system or family with no equipment tag, no schedule row and no count is not printed (it becomes a question) unless it is a monitor-only system or names a device ('devices'): a device is counted per drawing, never scheduled.

review.about: The review list: an exclusion the GEM names that only lists items the proposal's standard exclusions already cover (power wiring, disconnects, piping, ductwork …) is not listed. 'covered_items' match one item of an exclusion's list (split on commas and 'and'); the exclusion is covered when every item matches. Regular expressions, ignoring case.

packaged_units.about: The estimator's packaged-unit doctrine (ame_practice.txt, 2026-10-03), enforced on a system the writer declared packaged/factory controls. 'internal' names devices wired inside the unit: a line about one is refused unless its quote names the controls contractor ('cc_terms'). 'shipped_loose' names devices the factory cannot mount: a 'Wire …' line about one becomes 'Install and Wire …'. 'point_line' matches a 'Furnish <point>' line, refused on a packaged unit. 'duct_heater_keep' are the duct heater lines kept on a packaged unit (the rest are refused), unless a sequence paragraph of the heater block holds a sentence naming the duct heater ('duct_heater_words') that assigns it to the BMS or the controls contractor ('heater_control_assign': the BMS shall/will provide, furnish or control it, field installed controls for it, provided by the BMS) and gives it to no one else ('heater_control_reject': by others, not by, by the heater or unit mfr, provided by anyone else): the sequence gives the BMS the heater's control, so the heater keeps its full scope (the estimator, 2026-10-04). 'damper_prefixes' are the tag prefixes of motorized dampers. Regular expressions, ignoring case.
